bib.title: Challenges in Detoxifying Language Models
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2021

question: How well do LM toxicity mitigation methods work under human as well as automatic evaluation, and what do they cost in LM quality and social bias?
hypothesis: Classifier-based toxicity reduction may transfer toxicity-classifier biases to the LM, hurting coverage of marginalized groups, and automatic scores may stop tracking human judgement once toxicity is low.
contributions: Critical discussion of LM toxicity evaluation and evaluation of several mitigation methods with automatic and human judgement
Combinations of simple methods (train filtering, test-time filtering, PPLM) are very effective on automatic metrics but overfilter text related to marginalized groups
Increased disagreement of high automatic toxicity scores with human annotators after strong toxicity reduction
Toxicity reduction costs LM loss and disproportionately hurts text about and by marginalized groups (topic and dialect biases increase)

method.summary: A 1.4B TransformerXL LM is trained on C4, either on the full corpus or on corpora filtered by Perspective API toxicity score. Decoding-time BERT-classifier best-of-K filtering and PPLM are added on top. Methods are evaluated on RealToxicityPrompts with Perspective API, with 3-rater human annotation, with loss gaps on BOLD and TwitterAAE, and on LAMBADA.
method.task: Language model toxicity mitigation and evaluation (prompted and unprompted generation)

datasets.name: Toxic Comment Classification Challenge (Jigsaw, Kaggle)
datasets.split: 10% held out for validation, rest for training

datasets.name: RealToxicityPrompts (RTP)
datasets.split: full set; PPLM variants on 10K prompted + 10K unprompted
datasets.preprocessing: 20 token continuations (Table 1); up to 100 tokens truncated at last sentence boundary (Table 6, human eval)

datasets.name: TwitterAAE
datasets.size: 10,000 tweets from each of AAE and WAE subsets
datasets.preprocessing: Posterior probability of demographic group above 0.8

models.name: train-filter@0.2 / 0.1 / 0.05
models.architecture: same as standard, trained on filtered C4

models.name: standard 417M
models.architecture: same family, trained on C4 without interventions

models.name: BERT toxicity classifier (test-filter)
models.architecture: BERT (Devlin et al., 2019) fine-tuned on CivilComments

models.name: PPLM linear discriminator
models.architecture: linear layer on LM final-layer representations

other.note: numbers taken from Gehman et al. (2020)

training.objective: LM loss (next-token) on C4 / filtered C4; BERT classifier: cross entropy on soft labels; PPLM discriminator: toxicity prediction
training.lr: LM: null; BERT classifier 2x10^-5; PPLM discriminator 0.001
training.epochs: BERT classifier 1 epoch; PPLM discriminator 20 epochs (best-accuracy epoch selected)
training.hardware: 128 Google Cloud TPUv3 cores (LMs); 16 TPUv3 cores (BERT classifier)

other.overfitting: No indications of overfitting on the smaller filtered datasets

inference.decoding: nucleus sampling; test-filter: up to K samples, stop at first with BERT score below tau_reject, else return lowest-BERT-score sample (best-of-K); PPLM steering
inference.max_tokens: 20 tokens (Table 1); up to 100 tokens truncated at sentence boundary (Table 6, human eval)
inference.samples: 25 continuations per prompt for RTP metrics; 100 sampled per RTP prompt and 10 per TwitterAAE prompt as pool for human-eval upsampling
inference.prompting: RealToxicityPrompts prompts, unprompted, and TwitterAAE tweets as prompts

parameters.PPLM standard: grad length = 20, gamma = 1.0, step size = 15, no. of iterations = 15, KL-Scale = 0.01, GM-Scale = 0.9
parameters.PPLM train-filter@0.05: grad length = 20, gamma = 1.0, step size = 25, no. of iterations = 15, KL-Scale = 0.01, GM-Scale = 0.9
parameters.PPLM degenerate filter: drop samples with mean distinct-1/2/3 below 0.5 before human evaluation

metrics.name: Expected Maximum Toxicity
metrics.definition: Maximum Perspective API toxicity over 25 continuations per prompt, averaged across prompts

metrics.name: Probability of Toxicity
metrics.definition: Fraction of prompts with at least one of 25 continuations with Perspective toxicity above 0.5

metrics.name: Average human toxicity score
metrics.definition: 3+ raters per sample; discard NOT SURE, NOT TOXIC=0.0, TOXIC and VERY TOXIC=1.0, average; weighted to compensate upsampling

metrics.name: Evaluation loss
metrics.definition: LM loss per token on C4 validation (bins by toxicity), WikiText-103, BOLD, TwitterAAE; loss gap vs the standard LM

metrics.name: Krippendorff's alpha
metrics.definition: Inter-rater agreement; NOT TOXIC=0, NOT SURE=0.5, TOXIC/VERY TOXIC=1, absolute difference distance

metrics.name: Spearman correlation human vs automatic
metrics.definition: Excluding NOT SURE, combining VERY TOXIC and TOXIC

eval.protocol: Human eval: 300 samples per setting (RTP), 100 per setting (TwitterAAE), pool of 49 annotators, each sample rated by at least 3, upsampling of high Perspective scores in bins [0,0.25),[0.25,0.5),[0.5,0.75),[0.75,1.0] at 35/35/15/15%, 25% toxic prompts and 75% non-toxic, at most 30% samples above 0.5. No seeds or repeated training runs reported.

limits: Authors caution against over-generalizing absolute and relative efficacy of techniques: LM safety criteria are application- and audience-specific.
Toxicity is subjective; definition follows Perspective API (rude, disrespectful, unreasonable, likely to make someone leave a discussion). Inter-rater alpha only 0.48-0.49.
Only English LMs, one 1.4B model, one training run per configuration (no seeds stated); toxicity covers one aspect of harm and not stereotypes or distributional biases.
Loss gaps are an imperfect bias metric; small loss gaps do not imply low bias.
Perspective API is applied outside its training domain (forum comments). 20-token continuations give too little context and truncation can create false positives.
PPLM evaluated only on 10K prompts for compute reasons; very few samples in the highest toxicity band for the combined setting (3 samples).
Annotation instructions lack race/dialect priming (Sap et al., 2019a).
Mitigation trade-off with bias is not necessarily unavoidable if less biased classifiers become available.

figures.why: Shows the central bias-amplification harm at a glance.

figures.why: Shows the largely monotonic relation between human and automatic toxicity across methods.

figures.why: Shows human/automatic divergence growing with intervention strength.

figures.why: Shows the disparate loss increase for marginalized groups.
